elements.element: Customer owns Deliverables and work product created for Customer.
elements.evidence: Retained 11.1.1.4 first sentence is untouched: "SFJ shall be the sole and exclusive owner of the Trial Data Package including the Research Results included therein." PB (Customer) acquires ownership only later, on payment of the Approval Payments plus a further purchase price under the Exhibit K mechanic.

elements.element: Vendor assigns the Deliverables and work product to Customer.
elements.evidence: 14.3.1 remains conditional: "such assignment to be effective in accordance with Section 11.1.1.4", i.e. contingent on the purchase mechanic; there is no present vesting of the Trial Data Package in PB.

elements.element: Vendor retains its pre-existing intellectual property.
elements.evidence: 11.1.1.1 is retained unchanged: "each Party will retain all right, title and interest in, to and under all Intellectual Property that is Controlled by such Party as of the Effective Date."

elements.element: Customer's licence to Vendor IP embedded in Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: No Customer-owned Deliverables exist under the redline, so there is no embedded-Vendor-IP licence structure; the new grant is a perpetual licence to SFJ-owned Trial Data Package, not a licence back of Vendor IP embedded in Customer-owned deliverables.

elements.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: Same structural gap: ownership of the work product stays with SFJ, so the preferred embedded-IP licence-back does not arise; the new clause grants an irrevocable licence to the SFJ-owned data package instead.

elements.element: Customer's licence to embedded Vendor IP is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: No Customer-owned Deliverable exists; the royalty-free wording attaches to the licence over the SFJ-owned Trial Data Package, not to Vendor IP embedded in Customer deliverables.

elements.element: Customer retains all rights in Customer Data.
elements.evidence: The Trial Data Package (all Information generated by or on behalf of either Party in the Clinical Trials, per 1.1.193) is owned outright by SFJ under retained 11.1.1.4; PB holds only a licence.

elements.element: Any Vendor licence in Customer Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services.
elements.evidence: New sentence: "SFJ shall use the Trial Data Package, including all Research Results, solely to perform its obligations and exercise its rights expressly set out in this Agreement, and shall not disclose, license, transfer, sell or otherwise exploit the Trial Data Package for any other purpose." This removes any independent exploitation, distribution or resale right.

elements.element: The parties do not jointly own intellectual property.
elements.evidence: No joint-ownership language appears in the cited or rendered text; 11.1.1.1 and 11.1.1.4 allocate sole ownership to one Party in each case, and the redline creates no co-ownership.

elements.element: Vendor may retain ownership of generic tools and know-how.
elements.evidence: 11.1.1.1 retained: each Party "will retain all right, title and interest in, to and under all Intellectual Property that is Controlled by such Party as of the Effective Date", which preserves SFJ's pre-existing tools and know-how.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: Inserted: "SFJ hereby grants to PB a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free license ... to use and modify the Trial Data Package, including all Research Results, for PB's business." The Trial Data Package is the trial work product at issue.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: Inserted grant is expressly "perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free"; nothing in the retained purchase mechanic conditions or terminates the licence.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is worldwide.
elements.evidence: Inserted grant is expressly "worldwide" with no territorial carve-out elsewhere in the rendered text.

elements.element: Customer's licence to Deliverables is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: Inserted grant is expressly "royalty-free"; the retained Approval Payments and Exhibit K purchase price relate to the transfer of ownership, not to the licence.

elements.element: Customer may use and modify Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: Inserted: licence "to use and modify the Trial Data Package, including all Research Results, for PB's business."

elements.element: Customer may sublicense Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: Inserted: licence "with the right to sublicense through multiple tiers", within the same "for PB's business" scope.

elements.element: Any Vendor licence in Customer Data is limited to processing it solely to provide the Services.
elements.evidence: Inserted second sentence confines SFJ to use "solely to perform its obligations and exercise its rights expressly set out in this Agreement" and bars any disclosure, licensing, transfer, sale or other exploitation for any other purpose.

elements.element: Customer may sublicense Deliverables for its business.
elements.evidence: Duplicate check: the multi-tier sublicense right is granted once, in the single inserted sentence; no duplicated operative grant elsewhere.

reasons: Fallback level is complete: the single inserted licence sentence supplies all five licence attributes (perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, use/modify/sublicense for PB's business) over the Trial Data Package, and the second inserted sentence supplies the service-limited-use restriction on SFJ.

Preferred level is not reached and the finding correctly targets the fallback: retained 11.1.1.4 keeps SFJ as sole and exclusive owner of the Trial Data Package and 14.3.1's assignment remains effective only "in accordance with Section 11.1.1.4", so there is no present vesting or assignment to PB and PB does not retain rights in its own trial data.

Minimality holds: SFJ's ownership, the Approval Payments, the further purchase price and the Exhibit K purchase mechanic are all left intact, nothing outside the two inserted sentences is deleted or paraphrased, and no survival tail, expense, remedy or procedural boilerplate is added. "Through multiple tiers" is a borderline but directly implements the sublicense element rather than adding a new requirement.

Intent is preserved: the insertion sits inside 11.1.1.4 without creating an undefined term or dangling cross-reference; SFJ's obligation to sell and transfer under 11.1.1.4 and its rights under 14.3.1 are expressly permitted uses under the new restriction, so no retained sentence is contradicted.

Drafting improvement (not a failure): the restriction permits SFJ to "exercise its rights expressly set out in this Agreement", and SFJ's ownership right is itself set out in the same section, which leaves a circularity argument that ownership permits exploitation. Consider tightening to "solely to perform its express obligations under this Agreement and for no other purpose" to close that reading.

Optional strengthening if SFJ pushes back on the licence: seek an express statement that the licence survives termination of the Agreement and any failure to complete the Exhibit K purchase, so the perpetual/irrevocable wording cannot be argued away by the retained purchase mechanic.
